call_points.text: EBITDA expected to stay under pressure for the next couple of quarters until global crises normalise.
Polymer capacity being built to take turnover from ₹1,000 Cr to about ₹2,000 Cr.
Disc brakes and switches start to matter only from FY28; disc brake production has started for one major Indian OEM.
M&A paused for a year to avoid stressing the balance sheet during the capex cycle and demerger.
Rupee at an all-time low against the dollar raises import costs for electronic child parts; management flags it could weaken further.
BMS is being exited; no further money will be invested as OEMs have decided to control it in-house.
Management guided for a major capex cycle of ₹680-700 crores in FY27 to cater to new business wins.

guidance.statement: Revenue target of ₹8,000 Cr for Calendar Year 2030 / FY31, from primarily organic and some inorganic growth
Polymer capacity to support about ₹2,000 Cr turnover from current ₹1,000 Cr
DICVS to grow at least 5% above market; ACFMS 10% above market

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,099.21 Cr, net profit ₹73.23 Cr (+109.5% YoY).
Pricol reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,078 Cr with PAT of ₹73.23 Cr and announced leadership transitions.
Pricol Limited shared the audio recording link for its Investor Conference Call on May 15, 2026, discussing audited Q4FY26 and FY26 results.
Pricol reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,077.9 Cr and PAT of ₹73.23 Cr, announcing a major ₹680-700 Cr capex plan for FY27 amidst macro headwinds.

On 31 July 2026 Pricol's Q1FY27 call reported revenue of ₹1,083.58 Cr (+23.46% YoY), EBITDA of ₹123.69 Cr at 11.41% margin and PAT of ₹67.02 Cr (+34.34%), with management flagging cost headwinds and a ₹700 Cr capex cycle.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval for appointment of Ms. Madhura Mohan and Mr. Siddharth Manoharan
Demerger approvals from SEBI, ROC and NCLT

watchlist.response: Chairman said it is in line with industry seasonality (Q4 high, Q1 drops) and the company grew above market in each division.
watchlist.text: Sequential revenue was flattish despite strong YoY growth; analysts asked which businesses dragged.

watchlist.response: Chairman said the DIS business needs large investment and technology partners, and a combined entity struggled to attract the right investors.
watchlist.text: Analysts pressed on the demerger rationale, given the core cluster business becomes a single-product entity.

watchlist.response: Chairman said at minimum four quarters, hoped for 12 months, citing dependence on SEBI, ROC and NCLT; no firm date given.
watchlist.text: Analysts asked for a demerger timeline.

watchlist.response: Chairman said real revenues only kick in from FY28; no quarterly figure given.
watchlist.text: Analysts asked for disc brake revenue and ramp-up.
